content:
According to a recent report from Bloomberg, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop. The company is reportedly "developing prototypes" but has not yet decided whether to ultimately launch the product.

The internal prototypes are reported to feature "a slim fabric strap with a computing module containing sensors built in." The project is currently in the "technology exploration" phase, and Bloomberg noted it would not launch until 2028 at the earliest, and only if Apple ultimately decides to release it.

The project is said to have the support of Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October after Jeff Williams stepped down.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who don't want to wear a smartwatch but still want to track their health and fitness. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing for an IPO and recently disclosed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the twelve months ending June 30; revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion in the nine months ending June 30.

However, Apple still dominates the smartwatch market. The Apple Watch also offers far more features than health and fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
